headline: Deep models translate across omics layers and read chromatin contact maps natively
label: Multimodal Omics And Chromatin Learning
summary: New models infer proteins, isoforms, chromatin and transcriptomes from partial omics, while Hi-C methods drop imputation and cut parameters.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned cross-modal translation and integration. TSNR predicts spatial protein abundance from spatial transcriptomics. IsoPrism allocates isoform proportions from short-read single-cell and spatial data. Top2All reconstructs transcriptome-wide expression from sparse high-expression genes. MUTUAL aligns frozen foundation-model embeddings into a shared RNA-ATAC space trained on 3.0M multiome cells. MAD conditionally edits nucleus images and expression jointly. At tissue scale, CORAL (graph-attention generative model) and DIRAC (geometric domain adaptation with label transfer) integrate multiscale or cross-study spatial multi-omics. A second, smaller thread treats Hi-C matrices as native inputs. scSTEC annotates subcompartments from individual scHi-C matrices without imputation or cross-cell information. AxialTAD predicts TAD boundaries with 76-80% fewer parameters than deepTAD. C-Fetch retrieves contact-map features through reference-guided search in KL-regularized 3D autoencoder space. Across both threads, the new element is inference from incomplete or single-modality inputs rather than reliance on dense paired measurements.
